args.name: moss-resting-pad-trial
args.function: Provide a learnable physical operation to attempt arranging owned moss into a small resting pad at a reachable site, retaining actual work progress and reporting whether a usable arrangement was achieved. Allow subsequent inspection and a real rest trial rather than granting a benefit on registration.
args.conditions: An owned moss sample remains: 0.9 unit. A press trial at intensity 0.3 reported held=false and flexibility=0.8. Suitability for bedding, necessary quantity, processing and durability are unknown. Work must use a reachable unoccupied footprint and stop safely if materials or conditions are insufficient.
args.inputs: Owned unreserved moss and a nominated reachable footprint; any additional necessary inputs must be identified before consumption, not invented.
args.costs: Method, learning time, work duration and material requirements are unknown; expose actual requirements and a cancellation contract before work begins.
args.effects: Produce only a physically supported trial arrangement and observations if successful. Any resting effect must depend on actual construction and testing; failure must report what prevented completion without claiming improvement.

candidates.function: Prepare a small soil patch and place one real root unit for a persistent observation trial; resume or cancel unfinished work.
candidates.costs: Plant: one owned unspoiled root unit; two work rounds at one energy each. Supply inputStackId and an unoccupied ordinary-soil x/y patch within 0.65 plus body radius. Resume/cancel use personal processId (omitting it selects the sole unfinished job). No tools or water are granted.
candidates.effects: Preparation and exact escrow persist when other actions interrupt work. Resume pays only remaining work. Cancel releases surviving unplanted material once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort and spoiled material are never refunded. Completed plots retain the real reserved root while existing environmental ageing runs. Reinspect with baseline probe: 30 elapsed rounds mark an inconclusive observation interval, not maturity or inferred death. There is no propagation, tending or harvest rule in this precursor, and no reward for placing it. Genuine observed changes can use existing evidence-deduplicated probe feedback. Other people can observe the actual plot; execution requires personal study.

candidates.function: Record a planted-root baseline, observe, or physically uncover and cover an existing specimen while retaining actual progress and private evidence.
candidates.costs: Begin/observe: one round and 0.2 energy. Inspect: two paid work rounds, one energy each, no consumed root or tools. Only the creator may handle a plot; anyone may observe reachable public state. Provide target plot ID; resume/cancel can use exact personal processId.
candidates.effects: Begin records an external baseline and claims a personal work lock. Inspect uncovers the existing reserved root, records actual present condition, then replaces displaced soil. Interruption retains exposure and paid work; resume completes outstanding work only. Cancel/death releases the lock without automatically covering or refunding effort. Existing specimen ageing continues while unattended. Repeated unchanged observations and the 30-round checkpoint create no reward. No inferred germination, tending benefit, harvested food or biomass is supplied. Relevant dated physical changes may use the single existing grounded-understanding rule. Records remain personal until actual communication.

candidates.function: Physically examine one reachable x/y footprint and report visible surface evidence plus provisional compatibility with the existing root-placement operation.
candidates.costs: One completed round and 0.5 energy after valid visible reach and bounds checks. No material, tools, plot or reservation. Invalid invocations do not begin or charge. A later new examination pays again.
candidates.effects: Private dated surface/clearance findings identify operation limitations separately from unknown physical properties. Bare ground is distinct from the general ordinary-soil moisture regime. No deeper substrate, concealed occupant or hidden resource information. No clearing, excavation, sampling, planting, material change, skill grant, food or reward. The atomic attempt has no resumable work or maintenance; no unperformed completion is recorded. Results are not silently refreshed and sharing requires real communication.

candidates.function: Travel toward a self-chosen coordinate or known object/item using observed obstacles.
candidates.costs: Actual distance times 2, increased by carried mass; speed 0.8 per simulation time unit.
candidates.effects: Continues until within the target interaction area or a real failure. Empty target uses x/y. A resource:ID target selects only a remembered ground stack.

candidates.function: Recover available physical energy at the current position.
candidates.effects: Base recovery 4, modified by actually accessible registered facilities; capped at 40.

candidates.function: Transfer a nearby ground stack into personal inventory.
candidates.effects: Requires actual distance within pickup reach; resource:ID means a matching nearby visible ground stack.
Actual nutrition and toxicity apply. Food never directly heals. resource:ID selects an owned stack.

candidates.function: Place owned units on the ground.
candidates.effects: Other actors may subsequently collect the ground stack.

packet.access: Search or retrieve only this experiment abilities with control queries. Missing candidates do not prove a function absent. Full implementation facts remain available in the development handoff; never grant inventory or individual mastery. Require actual physical prerequisites.
